story: On a breezy, clear Friday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary has stepped out onto Magnolia Loop, restless as ever, while Donna packs extra paddles and balls into her pickleball bag for his third-shot drop drills. Down the street, Hal reads the Halloween flyer and the new notices on the bulletin board with a reflective air. Back at her kitchen, Rosa is content, baking a batch of treats for Saturday's trick-or-treaters and the parade crowd.
events: Gary headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Donna (donna pickleball bag): Pack extra paddles and balls for Gary's third-shot drop drills
Hal (street bulletin board): Read the Halloween flyer and any new notices posted on the board
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Bake a batch of treats for Saturday's trick-or-treaters and parade crowd

gary.thought_process: It's Friday morning, the parade is tomorrow evening, and approval still hasn't come through. Rosa and Donna have been helping, and I've already rechecked the harness and tested the speaker quietly. The install kit is packed. Nothing left to do at the bench that I haven't done three times over, and I won't touch the cart until Architectural Review signs off. Best use of this hour is to walk over to Magnolia Loop and see if anyone's around, then check on the application status. Sitting here staring at a labeled harness won't speed the committee up, and I'd feel more useful out among people.

parameters.content: Kit's packed and the bench work is done. Heading out to the Loop to see who's around and whether word's come back on my cart application.

donna.thought_process: I checked the calendar last tick, so no need to repeat that. Nobody's here, and it's Friday morning before Halloween. Gary and I need third-shot drop practice before the ladder match, and he's the one who hasn't played before. Best move is to grab my pickleball bag and get ready, then head out to find Gary and the courts. Packing the bag is concrete progress toward the ladder climb.

parameters.content: Pack extra paddles and balls for Gary's third-shot drop drills

hal.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop at quarter past eight with nobody around. Donna's already given me her word on three flamingos, and Gary seems to be keeping his work in the garage. I've been standing on this street logging things long enough, and I'm starting to suspect I care more about being right than being neighborly. The bulletin board has that Halloween flyer posted, and there may be a fresh notice or two I ought to read. A quick look at the board is a reasonable, orderly use of the morning, and it keeps me from just glaring at the neighbors' lawns.

parameters.content: Read the Halloween flyer and any new notices posted on the board

rosa.thought_process: I'm home at Rosa's House on Friday morning, nobody nearby. Last tick I checked my shift schedule to confirm Saturday evening is clear for the parade. The review desk walk is Thursday and already done, and the clamp list and light layout are in the folder. What's left is prep for Saturday: Halloween on the Loop, parade at 6. The kitchen is right here, so I can bake something for the trick-or-treaters and the neighbors who come by the cart. Rather than wander off with nobody around to talk to, I'll do something useful with the kitchen and keep my hands busy.

parameters.content: Bake a batch of treats for Saturday's trick-or-treaters and parade crowd

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
